messages:
Alex Chen: Quick heads-up — we're seeing a small regressed tail on H100 when the kernel arbiter prefers the Triton path for medium sequence bursts (seqlen ~= 512, batch 1-4). Profiler + traces below.

Jia Patel: Can you paste the perf numbers and the probe trace? Is this consistent across models?

Alex Chen: Paste from a quick run:
```
model: rw-variant-qlora
hw: h100
workload: microburst (3 short requests back-to-back)
route: autotuned -> Triton
p50: 9.8ms
p95: 38.2ms
p99: 67.4ms
cutlass (forced): p50: 7.1ms p95: 25.6ms p99: 48.9ms
nvtx: many small kernel launches on Triton path, bigger fused kernel on CUTLASS
```
kv cache note: warm KV hits ~0.25, warmup improves CUTLASS more than Triton in this profile.

Rajiv "Raj" Menon: Interesting. Could be probe sampling bias — the autotuner's probe plan used sequences sampled from long-running tails, not the microburst pattern. Do we still record per-probe batch size / kv-hit ratio? 

Alex Chen: We do, but the probe weight for microburst patterns is tiny. Probes currently mostly reflect our synthetic distribution (avg batch 8, seqlen 256). Microburst (batch 1-4) underrepresented.

Sam Ortega: Quick mitigation: add a forced canary routing rule for seqlen>=384 && avg_batch<=4 && kv_hit_rate<=0.4 -> prefer CUTLASS. We can push as transient to see impact.

Jia Patel: Agreed. Also propose improving the autotuner: include a feature vector [avg_batch, kv_hit_rate, seqlen, is_prefix_cached] and train a light-weight decision tree on probe outcomes. Hysteresis needed to avoid flip-flopping.

Alex Chen: I'll run a 1hr canary in us-west with the forced rule and collect token-level traces + nvprof. Can someone add a telemetry tag `probe_source=microburst` to the probe jobs so we can slice by probe type?

perf-bot: Canary rule applied to 10% of hostpool us-west (rule id: cr-20260317-01). Telemetry tag `probe_source=microburst` added to probe jobs.

Rajiv "Raj" Menon: Post-canary checklist:
- compare p50/p95/p99 for both paths
- check kernel_launch_count and avg_kernel_duration
- KV hit impact: simulate cold vs hot cache
- update autotuner weightings and re-run offline sims

Alex Chen: Thanks. If results show consistency we'll fold the rule into the arbiter as a feature-based override and add a soft penalty for switching (10% hysteresis window). I'll post results in ~90m.

Sam Ortega: Also adding a note: watch out for quantized kernels on CUTLASS that sometimes degrade quality at extreme seqlen. Add evals to the canary.

Alex Chen: Good call. Adding eval run to canary. Will update thread with numbers.
